target.title: fix(cost): align token usage refresh cadence with global settings
target.body:
### Summary
Fixes #2103.

Aligns the token/cost auto-refresh cadence with the configured global refresh settings instead of keeping them governed by a separate, hardcoded hourly TTL.

### Background / Problem
Previously, when the global refresh frequency was configured to a shorter interval (e.g., every minute), the main provider usage refresh followed that setting, but the token/cost data remained governed by a separate fixed `tokenFetchTTL` of 1 hour. This caused the widget/UI to display fresh quota data alongside stale token/cost metrics, creating a mismatch in auto-refresh frequency.

### Proposed Changes
- **Dynamic tokenFetchTTL (`Sources/CodexBar/UsageStore.swift`)**: Replaced the hardcoded hourly constant `tokenFetchTTL` with a dynamic property that retrieves the nominal interval from `settings.refreshFrequency`.
- **Timer and Observer Sync (`Sources/CodexBar/UsageStore.swift`)**: Updated the settings observation loop to call `startTokenTimer()` upon configuration changes, ensuring that updating the refresh frequency immediately applies to the background token refresh timer.
- **Dynamic Preferences UI (`Sources/CodexBar/PreferencesMenuPane.swift`)**: Replaced the static "hourly" auto-refresh text under cost settings with a localized string formatted dynamically using the user's active global frequency label, preventing UI text and execution behavior divergence.
- **Regression Tests (`Tests/CodexBarTests/UsageStoreTokenTTLReproductionTests.swift`)**: Added comprehensive tests validating dynamic TTL logic, verification of cooldowns, and setting transitions.

### Verification Results
- Added new test suite `UsageStoreTokenTTLReproductionTests` and ran successfully on macOS.
- Local lint checks (`swiftlint` and `swiftformat`) all passed cleanly.
